What is Tabnine?

Privacy-first AI coding assistant aimed at regulated and IP-sensitive organisations. Its differentiator is deployment flexibility - fully air-gapped on-premises or VPC installation with models that provably never see your code leave your infrastructure.

Best for

AI coding assistance where code absolutely cannot leave the organisation's network.

Main features

  • Air-gapped, on-premises and VPC deployment options
  • models trained only on permissively licensed code with provenance attribution
  • personalisation on your own codebase without sending it to a vendor
  • Tabnine Chat and agents for code review, test generation, documentation and Jira-to-code
  • switchable models (Tabnine's own, Claude, GPT, Mistral)
  • admin controls and audit
  • IP indemnification on enterprise tiers.

Practical use cases

  • Providing AI assistance to developers who are contractually barred from sending code to third-party clouds
  • generating tests and documentation inside an air-gapped network
  • enforcing that no proprietary code trains a vendor model
  • satisfying auditors on code provenance.

Who is it for?

  • Banks, defence, healthcare, government and any organisation with strict data-residency, IP or compliance requirements.

Pricing, free access & limits

Per-seat subscription; enterprise self-hosted licensing

Plans described in the source

Dev tier around $9/user/mo (billed annually) for individuals and small teams. Enterprise around $39/user/mo (annual, typically with seat minimums) adding self-hosted/air-gapped deployment, SSO, admin controls, IP indemnification and private model personalisation. A free tier with basic completions has existed but has been narrowed over time. Verify current tiers directly.

Free plan

Limited - a basic free tier has existed historically but the current offering centres on paid plans. Verify.

Free trial

Yes - free trials offered on Dev and Enterprise (typically 14-30 days).

Usage limits to consider

Self-hosted deployment requires meeting hardware specifications (GPU requirements for local models). Some agent features and model choices are enterprise-only. Seat minimums typically apply to Enterprise.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The only credible fully air-gapped option in this group - for regulated environments that is not a preference but a requirement
  • provenance-attributed training data and IP indemnification address a real legal exposure
  • very broad IDE coverage including older editors
  • strong admin and audit controls.

Limitations to consider

  • Raw code-generation quality trails Cursor and Copilot, particularly on agentic multi-file work
  • self-hosting carries meaningful infrastructure cost and operational burden
  • the free tier has been progressively reduced
  • smaller ecosystem and community
  • enterprise pricing is high per seat for the capability delivered.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • VS Code, JetBrains suite, Visual Studio, Eclipse, Neovim, Vim, Emacs, Android Studio
  • self-hosted server on Kubernetes/Docker

Languages

  • 80+ programming languages

API access

Enterprise APIs for admin and integration; self-hosted model endpoints

Integrations and exports

  • Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Atlassian, Jenkins, internal SCM via self-hosted connectors

Evaluation notes

Choose Tabnine for the compliance posture, not for the code quality - if your organisation can send code to a vendor cloud, Copilot or Cursor will produce better results for less. Validate GPU sizing before committing to air-gapped deployment.
